convertArchivedExportToFormat builds a shell command string by interpolating the user-controlled outputPreset (route param $preset) and fileName (query param 'run') and executes it with spawn(command, [], { shell: true }). A crafted preset such as 'xlsx; cat /etc/passwd' executes arbitrary shell commands.

renderPolicyForBindery passes the layoutProfile (taken from the 'x-bindery-profile' request header in app.policies.$id.bindery.tsx:23) directly into an execSync shell string. A header value like 'plain; touch /tmp/pwned' injects arbitrary commands.

previewProratedStartingPay compiles a user-supplied formula (from the 'formula' query param in app.compensation.proration-preview.tsx:15) via new Function('principal','days', `return ${formula};`). This executes arbitrary JavaScript server-side (remote code execution).

fetchEmployeeProfileCard returns the full employee row (including ssnLast4, phone, address, internalNote) and the loader only calls requireUser with no object-level authorization check. Any authenticated user (including a plain employee) can enumerate any employee id and retrieve another employee's PII and internal HR notes.

loadCompensationRecordEntry loads any compensation record by id and the loader only calls requireUser without verifying the caller is allowed to view that employee's salary/bonus history. Any signed-in user can enumerate salary and bonus data for any employee.

queryEmployeeDirectory interpolates the user-controlled searchTerm directly into an LDAP filter `(cn=*${searchTerm}*)` without escaping. Unlike findUserByEmail (which uses escapeLdapFilterValue), this path is vulnerable to LDAP filter injection, allowing a caller to modify the query structure. The value is sourced from the 'q' query param in app.admin.directory-sync.tsx:19-20.

readArchivedExportRun reads fs.readFile(path.join(ARCHIVE_DIR, fileName)) with no basename/path validation. The fileName comes directly from the 'run' route parameter (app.admin.exports.archive.$run.tsx:12-17), so a value like '../../.env' reads arbitrary files outside the archive directory.

loadPolicyTemplate joins the user-controlled fileName (from the 'template' query param or cookie in app.admin.policies.tsx:30-34) with TEMPLATES_DIR without any basename or allowlist check (unlike loadOnboardingTemplate which guards both). A value like '../../.env' reads arbitrary files.

saveDepartmentLetterhead builds a filename from file.name (the uploaded filename, user-controlled) and writes it via path.join(BRANDING_DIR, fileName) with no sanitization. A filename containing '../' escapes the branding directory and writes files to arbitrary locations.

renderDocumentCoverSheet interpolates doc.title and doc.originalName (both user-controlled at upload time) directly into raw HTML, including inside a <script> block (var coverSheetTitle = "${doc.title}"), with no HTML/JS escaping. This is stored XSS triggered by any user who views the cover sheet (app.documents.$id.cover.tsx and app.documents.$id.widget.tsx).

renderAcknowledgementCertificatePrintout interpolates closingNote (and policyTitle/version) directly into HTML without escaping. closingNote is sourced from the user-controlled 'note' query param (app.policies.ack.$id.tsx:44), resulting in reflected XSS in the printout page.

documentCoverDispositionHeader interpolates the user-controlled doc.title directly into a Content-Disposition header without stripping CR/LF characters (contrast with policyCoverDispositionHeader which scrubs them). A title containing CRLF can inject additional response headers.

readCarrierAssertion parses the payload of a bearer token and trusts its claims (employeeId, tier, decision) without verifying the JWT signature. It is used by the unauthenticated benefits-carrier callback api.v1.requests.$id.eligibility-sync.tsx:20, so an attacker can forge an assertion like {decision:'approved', tier:'senior'} and resolve/alter benefits cases without a valid signature.
